title: Every element of a projectively infinite-rank module over a ring with Noetherian radical quotient lies in a finite stably free direct summand

standard_prerequisites.name: An element of a projective module that is not a zero divisor on the fibres generates a free direct summand after one passes to a suitable element of the module
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: invoked at proof lines 39126-39129, where the surjection onto the complement K' is used to find p with the image of (1, p) generating a free direct summand
standard_prerequisites.use: Produces the free summand that is split off from the complement inside R direct sum P.

standard_prerequisites.name: A projective module that is the kernel of a surjection onto a projective module is a direct summand, and being a direct summand of a projective module, hence projective
standard_prerequisites.use: Makes the kernel of the projection onto K'' a direct summand of P containing the given element s.

standard_prerequisites.name: Stable freeness is preserved by taking direct summands of finite free modules: if R direct sum N is isomorphic to a finite free module then N is stably free
standard_prerequisites.use: Concludes that the direct summand produced is finite stably free, which is the conclusion of the lemma.

core_obligations: Use the auxiliary result that an element of a projective module can be placed in a finite free direct summand of a finite free direct summand of a direct sum to reduce to the case where a finite stably free direct summand K of R direct sum P already contains (0, s) (proof lines 39116-39120).

Under that hypothesis choose a complement K' with R direct sum P = K direct sum K', note that the projection onto K' is surjective, and use the auxiliary splitting result to find p in P such that the image of (1, p) generates a free direct summand, so that K' = R pi(1, p) direct sum K'' (proof lines 39123-39130).

Show that the projection pi' from P onto K'' is surjective (the author supplies the computation in a footnote) and that it splits because K'' is projective, so that the kernel of pi' is a direct summand of P containing s (proof lines 39134-39144).

Identify R direct sum ker(pi') with K direct sum R pi(1, p), and conclude that ker(pi') is finite stably free because K is finite and stably free and R pi(1, p) is free, which is the required direct summand containing s (proof lines 39144-39149).
proof_roadmap: Reduce to the case where a finite stably free summand of R direct sum P already contains the given element, using the auxiliary lifting for projective modules (proof lines 39116-39120).
Split the complement by a free direct summand generated by the image of an element (1, p) chosen through the second auxiliary result (proof lines 39123-39130).

Observe that the projection onto the remaining summand K'' is split, take its kernel as the candidate summand of P containing s, and check that R direct sum this kernel is finite free (proof lines 39134-39149).
difficulty_reason: The statement places a single element s of a projective module P inside a finite stably free direct summand, under the hypotheses that the quotient of the ring by its Jacobson radical is Noetherian and that the localizations of P at all maximal ideals have infinite rank (statement lines 39107-39114). The proof is a two-stage reduction rather than a formal consequence of the hypotheses: it first uses an auxiliary lifting result to reduce to the case where a finite stably free summand of R direct sum P contains (0, s), and then, inside that case, chooses a complement K' and splits off a free summand from it by a second auxiliary result, so that the kernel of the remaining projection is a direct summand of P containing s whose sum with R is finite free (proof lines 39116-39149). The two steps use the two auxiliary lemmas of the same section, which are carried as navigation stubs; all the bookkeeping with the complements and the final stable freeness argument are inside the counted span.
